summary: A host-side num_warps 4->1 tune of _align_small_kernel at num_tokens<=8 is plausible, rules-clean, shape-disjoint from every other landed change, and readable from the per-kernel profile rows (1.4 us at bs=1, 2.7 us at bs=8 in job 3cabc739), though the headline (<1% at two of six loads) cannot resolve it.
justification: Profile 3cabc739f1af493e confirms the hypothesis's numbers: _align_small_kernel is 1.4 us (3.2%) at bs=1 and 2.7 us (2.2%) at bs=8, directly on the critical path before the w13 Marlin launch. The kernel is one program with a serial chain of tl.sum/tl.cumsum over tiny tensors (bs=1: BLOCK_N=8, CAP_BLOCK=256, MB_BLOCK=32, BSM=8; bs=8: BLOCK_N=64, CAP_BLOCK=512, MB_BLOCK=64, BSM=8). At 4 warps, any reduction or scan whose axis Triton's blocked layout splits across warps needs a shared-memory round trip and a bar.sync; at 1 warp everything is in-thread or shuffles. So the mechanism is plausible. Expected size: saving 0.2-0.9 us is 0.3-0.8% of the bs=1 and bs=8 shape times, which moves the geomean by about 0.1-0.25%. That is far inside the run's ±1.5% CI, so only the _align_small_kernel profile rows can judge it. Weakest link: the profile shape does not clearly point to sync cost. The kernel goes 1.4 us (bs=1, n=8) -> 2.7 us (bs=8, n=64) -> 2.8 us (bs=16, n=128). The jump from bs=1 to bs=8 goes with the [BLOCK_N, 32] one-hot growing from 256 to 2048 elements. That suggests per-element in-thread work (one-hot, two cumsums along axis 0, the onehot*seg_start and rank products), not only cross-warp sync. At 1 warp that work is 4x more serial per thread (64 elements per thread per [64,32] temporary, against 16 at 4 warps), so bs=8 could come out flat or slower even with no spills. bs=1 ([8,32] = 8 per thread at 1 warp) is the likelier winner. The expected directions are consistent with TASK.md: bs=16 and up are untouched because n=128 > 64 keeps num_warps=4, and the weights are equal across loads.
confounders: triton-map-align-on-block-m-restack: introduced _align_small_kernel with the fixed num_warps=4 that this change tunes. It is the change's subject, not a confounder. Its block_size_m pick (two smaller only at >=128 tokens) leaves BSM=8 at bs<=8, so the tuned variants are the same ones it measured.
align-parallel-per-expert-verify: only num_tokens > 32 (_align_parallel_kernel). Shape-disjoint, no interaction.

post-expert-norm-triton-small-m: a different kernel at the tail of the same small-m launch sequence. Its time does not depend on the align kernel's warp count, so no interaction beyond graph launch order.

sglang-marlin-path-parity: provides the Marlin consumers of sorted_ids/block_experts. Their contents are bit-identical under the change (same kernel, same outputs), so Marlin time cannot move because of it.
interference: No companion is warranted. The change is one scalar on one launch at shapes no other landed hypothesis touches, and the outputs are bitwise identical, so downstream kernels cannot change. Attribution is direct: compare the _align_small_kernel row at bs=1 and bs=8 against 1.4/2.7 us in 3cabc739f1af493e (and the same rows in 45eacf4ca2e849d2), with the bs=16 row (2.8 us, untouched variant) as the in-run control for profiler drift. A gain is unambiguous. A loss at bs=8 with n_spills=0 would mean in-thread serial work outweighs the saved syncs. That would naturally lead to a follow-up (num_warps=2 at n<=64, or 1 warp only at n<=8, i.e. bs=1 only), not a companion now, because the parent's single result already says which direction 1 warp goes at each size.
open_questions: _align_self_check covers _align_small only at tokens 1, 8, 16, 32. The 1-warp variants at tokens 2-7 (including the judge's bs=4 test, n=32) are compiled in warm-up but not checked against SGLang's align in prepare. The kernel body is unchanged, so the risk is low, but adding tokens=4 to the self-check shapes would cover the bs=4 test before the judge does.

If bs=1 improves and bs=8 does not, is the sync cost or the per-thread one-hot/cumsum work the dominant term at n=64? The n_regs/n_spills print plus the bs=8 row will tell. Consider num_warps=2 at 32 < n <= 64 as the follow-up.

Overlap with in-flight rewrites: cuda-fused-moe-bs1-persistent-w13-silu-w2 (bs=1) and cuda-fused-moe-midm-single-launch-routed (2..32) would retire this kernel at these shapes if they land. The gain here is worth landing only while _align_small remains on the bs<=8 path.
